observation: Revenue fell 2% to £393.3m while underlying operating profit rose 5%
Underlying operating margin improved from 13.6% to 14.6%
Cash conversion was 105% and net debt fell 45%
Company reported labour availability and supply-chain pressures likely to continue into 2022
Order book rose 5% and covered about 84% of expected 2022 revenue
Countermeasures margin improved due to stronger operational execution
Company planned continued modernisation automation and lean-manufacturing investment
Working capital stayed at 21% of revenue and absolute inventory fell
Revenue rose 12% and return on sales improved 200 basis points
Supply-chain disruption caused £10.3m of excess freight costs
Price rises covered raw-material costs but not all excess freight costs
Company announced a £28m capacity expansion operational from late 2022
Trade working capital to sales improved from 23.2% to 20.7%
Company expected inventory days to rise after deciding to build raw-material and finished-goods inventory
H1 cash conversion fell to 52% from 137% as working capital and capex increased
Management expected supply-chain disruption to remain a headwind throughout 2021
Ten-month group revenue was 3% above the prior year
Automotive revenue fell 6% because of industry supply-chain bottlenecks
Expected full-year revenue was cut by up to £10m because automotive recovery did not occur
Management characterised the automotive supply problem as transitory
General-industrial supply chains remained short of inventory
Cash flow remained strong and margins were described as healthy
Energy and labour inflation were being passed to customers
Existing restructuring savings were supporting margins
